title: Large Language Models
standfirst: How transformers scaled into today's LLMs — pre-training, fine-tuning, alignment, and the practical realities.

description_paragraphs: This course covers the Transformer architecture, pretraining and fine-tuning of language models, and different tokenizer types such as BPE, WordPiece, and SentencePiece. It also examines LLM architectures, common datasets, and challenges in handling long-context attention, and various fine-tuning techniques for large language models. This course is also offered as an elective for PG-diploma students.
faculty: Prof. Mitesh Khapra, Wadhwani School of Data Science, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Transformer architecture foundations; Self-attention mechanisms; Multi-head attention.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Decoder mechanisms (teacher forcing, masked attention); Positional encoding (including sinusoidal); Normalisation techniques (batch and layer normalisation).

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Language modelling fundamentals; Transformers for language modelling; Causal language modelling; Generative pre-trained transformers (GPT); Pre-training and fine-tuning.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Decoding strategies (greedy, beam search, sampling-top-k, top-p); BERT and masked language modelling; Next sentence prediction; Pre-training and adaptation to downstream tasks.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Tokenization challenges; Subword tokenization methods; Byte Pair Encoding (BPE); WordPiece and SentencePiece tokenizers.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Modern transformer models (BART, GPT-2); Prompting techniques; Model design choices and performance factors; Architectural and objective variations; Pre-training data scale; Fine-tuning strategies; Multi-task learning.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Scaling in language models; Data sourcing and cleaning; Preprocessing pipelines; Pre-training datasets and data considerations.

weeks_text.label: Week 11
weeks_text.text: Efficient attention mechanisms; Time and space complexity of attention; Local and sparse attention; Low-rank approximations; Fast inference techniques.

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: Positional encoding techniques; Relative position encoding; Rotary embeddings (RoPE); ALiBi and alternative positional methods.
